LVKE.|167}}</noinclude>there, your peace shal rest vpon him: but if not, it shal returne to you. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=7}}† And in the same house tarie you, eating and drinking such things as they haue. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''1. Tim. 5, 18.''}}* For the vvorkeman is vvorthie of his hire. Remoue not from house to house. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=8}}† And into vvhat citie soeuer you enter, and they receiue you, eate such things as are set before you: {{verse|chapter=10|verse=9}}† and cure the sicke that are in it, and say to them, The kingdom of God is come nigh vpon you.⊣

{{verse|chapter=10|verse=10}}† And into vvhatsoeuer citie you enter, and they receiue you not, going forth into the streates thereof, say, {{verse|chapter=10|verse=11}}† The dust also of your citie that cleaueth to vs, vve doe vvipe of against you. yet this knovv ye that the kingdom of God is at hand. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=12}}† I say to you, it shal be {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Differences of paines and damnation in Hel according to the differences of demerites. ''Aug. li. 5. c. 5. cont. Iulian''.}}∷ more tolerable for Sodom in that day, then for that citie. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=13}}† VVo to thee Corozáim, vvo to thee Beth-saida: for if in Tyre and Sidon had been vvrought the miracles that haue beene vvrought in you, they had done penance sitting {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ True penance not onely to lead a new life, but to punish the body by such things as here be recorded, for the il life past.}}∷ in sacke cloth and ashes long agoe. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=14}}† But it shal be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon in the iudgement, then for you. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=15}}† And thou Capharnaum that art exalted vnto heauen: thou shalt be thrust dovvne euen vnto hel. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=16}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel for many Martyrs.}}{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ It is al one to despise Christ, and to despise his Priests and Ministers in the the Catholike Church: to refuse his doctrine, & theirs.}}∷ He that heareth you, heareth me: and he that despiseth you, despiseth me. And he that despiseth me, despiseth him that sent me.

{{verse|chapter=10|verse=17}}† And the Seuentie-tvvo returned vvith ioy, saying, Lord, the Deuils also are subiect to vs in thy name. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=18}}† And he said to them, I savv Satan as a lightening fal from heauen. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=19}}† Behold, I haue giuen you povver to treade vpon serpents, and scorpions, and vpon al the povver of the enemie, and nothing shal hurt you. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=20}}† But yet reioyce not in this, that the spirits are subiect vnto you: but reioyce in this, that your names are vvritten in heauen.⊣

{{verse|chapter=10|verse=21}}† In that very houre he reioyced in spirit, and said, I confesse to thee O Father, Lord of heauen and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast reuealed them {{sup|‖}} to litle ones. Yea Father, for so hath it wel pleased thee. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=22}}† Al things are deliuered to me of my father. And no man knovveth vvho the Sonne is, but the Father: and vvho the Father is, but the Sonne, and to vvhom the Sonne vvil reueale. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=23}}† And turning to his Disciples, he said, Blessed are the eies that see the things that you see. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=24}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō the 12 Sunday after Pentecost.}}For I say to you, that many Prophets and Kings desired to see the things that you see, and saw them not: and to heare the<noinclude>{{rh|||things}}</noinclude>
